subject: orangutan
title: Young Orangutans Use Leaves to Sound Like Big Males

scenes.text: A small orangutan can sound as big as a huge male. It uses a leaf.
When an orangutan is scared, it makes a sharp sucking call, called a kiss-squeak.
A researcher recorded over a thousand of them from twenty-three wild orangutans in Borneo.
Some held a bundle of leaves in front of their mouths. The call came out deeper.
Pitch usually tracks body size, and the youngest have the highest. The leaves cut the pitch without making it louder.
In a dark, thick forest where you hear predators before you see them, a deep voice may be a disguise.

description:
A small orangutan can sound as big as a huge male. It uses a leaf.
Wild orangutans in Borneo hold leaves to their mouths during alarm calls, lowering the pitch of the sound.
Would a deeper voice scare you?
first_comment: A leaf for a bigger voice. What's the cleverest animal tool you know of?
